security_audit.summary: Most detections in SKILL.md are Markdown code spans or fixed documentation paths and are false positives. The runner intentionally executes a user-provided training command. The output writer also imports and executes a module outside the audited skill package, requiring stronger trust controls.

remediation.issue: The runner can execute any executable and arguments supplied through the command option.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show the parsed argument list, and support executable allowlists for unattended use.

remediation.issue: The output writer executes a Python module resolved outside the audited skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle the writer with the skill or use a pinned package with integrity verification before loading it.

content.value_statement: Training runs often lack consistent evidence and clear status. This skill executes a selected command and records logs, metrics, checkpoints, changes, and outcomes.
actual_capabilities: Executes a selected training command without shell interpolation inside a chosen repository.
Supports startup verification, short-run verification, full kickoff, and resume modes.
Captures standard output, standard error, exit status, launch failures, and timeout state.
Extracts recent epochs, steps, metrics, and checkpoint paths from training logs.
Compares Git status before and after execution to report changed, new, and deleted files.
Produces structured run evidence for standardized training summaries, logs, commands, and status files.
limitations: The skill requires a training command that has already been selected.
It does not install environments, download assets, design sweeps, or choose research goals.
Metric and checkpoint extraction uses log patterns and may miss unusual output formats.
The output writer depends on a shared module outside the standalone skill package.

use_cases.title: Verify Training Startup
use_cases.description: Run a selected command briefly and confirm that steps, metrics, and checkpoints begin appearing.

use_cases.title: Document Reproduction Runs
use_cases.description: Capture command, dataset, checkpoint, status, and repository changes for a controlled reproduction attempt.

use_cases.title: Monitor Resume Operations
use_cases.description: Resume from a known checkpoint and record whether progress continues within a bounded monitoring window.

prompt_templates.title: Check Training Startup
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify startup in [repository] using [command]. Monitor for [seconds] seconds and report steps, metrics, checkpoints, and blockers.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Short Verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Run [command] in [repository] for [seconds] seconds. Record dataset assumptions, changed files, latest step, metric, and checkpoint.

prompt_templates.title: Resume From a Checkpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume [command] from [checkpoint] in [repository]. Confirm progress, capture logs, and distinguish a successful resume from partial monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Kick Off a Documented Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Kick off [command] in [repository] using [dataset]. Preserve seed and configuration context, monitor for [seconds] seconds, and produce all evidence files.

output_examples.input: Startup verification with a two-minute monitoring window.
output: Status: partial because the monitoring window elapsed after step 24.
Evidence: validation accuracy reached 0.71 and a step 24 checkpoint appeared.
Repository changes: one new checkpoint and one updated training log.

output_examples.input: Resume a selected run from an existing checkpoint.
output: Status: success because the resumed process completed without an error.
Progress: training continued from epoch 4 to epoch 5.
Evidence: the report records the checkpoint, latest metric, command outcome, and touched files.

best_practices: Review and confirm the exact command, repository, dataset, and checkpoint before execution.
Use a short monitoring window before committing resources to a full run.
Verify parsed metrics and checkpoint paths against the original logs before drawing conclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill to explore unknown commands or autonomous experiment variants.
Do not treat startup success as evidence of complete reproduction.
Do not execute commands from untrusted repositories without isolation and explicit review.

faq.question: Does this skill choose the training command?
faq.answer: No. It expects a documented or selected command and focuses on controlled execution and evidence.

faq.question: Can it prepare the environment?
faq.answer: No. Environment setup, dependency installation, and asset downloads must be completed separately.

faq.question: Which run modes are supported?
faq.answer: It supports startup verification, short-run verification, full kickoff, and resume.

faq.question: What evidence does it capture?
faq.answer: It captures logs, status, steps, metrics, checkpoints, timeouts, blockers, and repository changes.

faq.question: How are repository changes detected?
faq.answer: The runner compares Git status snapshots taken before and after the training command.

faq.question: Are extracted metrics always reliable?
faq.answer: No. Extraction uses general log patterns, so unusual formats require manual verification.
